correctness.rationale: For any d>=2, convex compact (d-1)-dimensional base B and oblique apex (p,h) with h>0, translate so 0∈B. At dimensionless height u∈[0,1] of P+s(-P), the maximal horizontal slice is (1-u)B+s(-B)+up, and at u∈[-s,0] it is B+(s+u)(-B)+up; both are attained, and all other feasible coefficient pairs are nested in those because the two base dilation factors decrease with the auxiliary height variable and 0∈B. Fubini gives exactly h[∫_0^1 vol_m((1-u)B+s(-B))du+∫_0^s vol_m(B+t(-B))dt]. Divide by h vol_m(B)/d, expand each integral by the standard Minkowski polynomial, and use binomial identities to obtain coefficient C(d,k)(M_(k-1)+M_k)/vol_m(B) for every k=0..d, with M_-1=M_d=0. Brunn–Minkowski vol_m(aB+b(-B))>=vol_m(B)(a+b)^m yields lower envelope 2(1+s)^d-1-s^d, equality for s>0 only when B and -B are translates, i.e. B centrally symmetric; at s=0 all bases give equality. Classical Rogers–Shephard upper bound at s=1 is attained iff P is simplex, equivalently B simplex. Minkowski interpolation of bases and continuity realize every intermediate ordinary-difference-body ratio d>=3; d=2 endpoints coincide. In dimension 3 M1/A=(q-2)/2 gives cubic 1+(3q/2)(s+s²)+s³, q∈[4,6]. No finite numeric testing is substituted for this exact all-d proof.
residual_risks: The upper endpoint and equality for simplices are classical cited prior work, not a novel upper-bound theorem.

value.rationale: Pyramids are a canonical dimension-raising convex-body operation. Determining the entire unbalanced difference-body polynomial and all reflected mixed-volume coefficients of a pyramid from adjacent mixed volumes of its arbitrary base is a structural identity with clear use in the Godbersen/Rogers–Shephard setting. The exact lower envelope, rigidity and complete 3D q-profile follow as meaningful family-specific implications. The acknowledged universal sharp upper inequality is old, but the claimed lifting identity and base-dependent profile are not textbook restatements of it.
residual_risks: No new general Rogers–Shephard or Godbersen proof is claimed; originality contribution is family-specific identity and consequences.

limitations: Nondegenerate convex pyramids with d>=2, positive apex height, arbitrary convex base and s>=0.
At s=0 equality in lower bound is not characteristic of base central symmetry.
